en-US.description: Cue-based media playback and show control for live video
en-US.longDescription:
Deckboy is a native desktop application for video engineers, AV technicians and live
operators who need a reliable way to organise media, trigger cues, loop content and send
video to production displays.

Cues are arranged in a playlist with fades, loops and hold-last-frame behaviour, and sent
to dedicated fullscreen outputs with per-output area of interest, edge feathering and
warp or keystone correction. Output can leave the machine as NDI, SRT, RTMP, Blackmagic
SDI or SMPTE ST 2110, several at once. Playback is driven from a Stream Deck, Bitfocus
Companion, OSC, MIDI, Art-Net or LTC timecode.

It also converts media that will not play, reports codec, raster, frame rate and duration
for any file, normalises loudness to EBU R128, generates test patterns, and captures a
camera, window or screen as a cue. PDF, PowerPoint and Keynote decks import as one cue per
slide, with presenter and prompter views available as output types.
en-US.name: Deckboy
en-US.releaseNotes:
Thanks
- Cool-Colin on Reddit suggested the layer blend modes (0.99.426).
- Tim Cronin suggested the Final Cut-style timeline.
- On GitHub: joeladria found that the interface had no text on macOS (#6), larszu found that the Mac build had no text layers (#7), and FillmyMap found that Ctrl+Shift+Space did not stop all decks (#12).

Lessons
- Fixed: in the Presets lesson, Esc closed the lesson instead of the DASH. Esc now closes whatever is open first (DASH, settings, a menu); only an Esc that nothing else wants leaves a lesson.
- Fixed: thirteen lesson steps pointed at nothing, so there was no ring to show where to click. MENU and DASH steps lost their pointer; a cue in a playlist that was not on screen had none (the pointer now goes to its tab first); the scopes steps lost theirs while a scope was shown large; and edge blend could not be found when the settings page was scrolled below it.

Playlists
- A second playlist now appears beside the first as soon as you add it, when the window has room. Before, it hid behind a tab until you dragged the playlist column wider. If you drag the column narrower again, it stays the way you set it.

Themes
- 40 new themes, from Amber CRT and Teletext to Risograph, Deep Sea and Synthwave. Every one passes the same readability check as the old ones: no label is hard to read, and a warning never looks like an ordinary message.

Dashboard
- The DASH has a CLOSE button. Before, it closed only with Esc, Ctrl+D or a click outside it.

First run
Deckboy is free software and is not code-signed, so the OS does not recognise the publisher. One time only:
- macOS — if it says the app is damaged: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Deckboy.app
- Windows — SmartScreen may appear: More info → Run anyway
Deckboy is free, open-source cue-based media playback and show control for live video — clips, slides and live sources on one cue list, out to a screen, NDI, SRT or Blackmagic SDI, with a stream and a recording running at the same time and presenter view on its own display, driven from a Stream Deck, Bitfocus Companion, OSC, MIDI or LTC timecode.
